claim_summary: For the Euclidean unit ball \(B_2^3\), the original common-frame Kuhn-packet radius of the face-centered-cubic lattice \(D_3=\{z\in\mathbb Z^3:\sum z_i\equiv0\pmod2\}\) is \(\kappa(B_2^3,D_3)=1\); that of the body-centered-cubic dual lattice \(D_3^*=\mathbb Z^3\cup(\mathbb Z^3+(1/2,1/2,1/2))\) is \(\kappa(B_2^3,D_3^*)=\sqrt5/4\). Both equal the corresponding classical covering radii. Among unordered linearly independent triples (all frame orderings identify the same packet), exactly 24 frames attain the FCC value, precisely the root triples with squared norms \(2\) and pairwise inner-product multiset \(\{-1,-1,0\}\); exactly 8 attain the BCC value, precisely triples of half-cube-vertex vectors with every pairwise inner product \(-1/4\). Every optimum frame is a lattice basis. All optimal frames, including those generating proper sublattices a priori, are covered by the classification.
integrity: Analytic proof covers all independent lattice frames; exact-rational code supplements it. No independent validation or historical-priority certification is claimed.
scientific_limitations: Only the standard Euclidean ball with FCC and dual BCC in dimension three; priority of equivalent older formulations remains provisional; no extension to arbitrary lattices.
title: Sharp Kuhn-packet radii and all minimizing frames for \(D_3\) and \(D_3^*\)
